bull.t: Large design‑win pipeline and secured backlog
bull.b: A >$300M multi-year design‑win pipeline with ~44% already in production and a ~$22M backlog provides multi-period revenue visibility. Converting these wins into production volumes materially de-risks future revenue, smooths manufacturing cadence, and supports scalable unit economics over the next 2–3 years.

bull.t: Product momentum across Cat‑M, Cat‑1bis and RF transceivers
bull.b: Diversified product traction — broad Cat‑M adoption, nascent Cat‑1bis ramps and a high‑margin RF transceiver market — expands end‑market exposure beyond legacy licensing. This product mix diversification can sustain revenue growth and lift gross margins as higher‑ASP and defense/drone applications scale over multiple years.

bull.t: Convertible debt redeemed; capital structure simplified
bull.b: Eliminating convertible debt materially reduces future dilution risk, interest/convertible servicing complexity and refinancing pressure. A simplified, near debt‑free capital structure improves financial flexibility, lowering financing costs and enabling management to allocate resources to product ramps and path to operating cash‑flow breakeven.

bear.t: Persistent negative operating and free cash flow
bear.b: Sustained negative operating and free cash flow (roughly -$10M monthly normalized burn) with only modest cash on hand creates structural financing risk. Unless production ramps and cost reductions convert to positive cash generation, the firm likely needs external funding or asset monetization to sustain operations over the next several quarters.

Sequential and year‑over‑year revenue weakness plus a meaningful gross‑margin drop indicate pricing, mix and input‑cost pressures. Persistent top‑line volatility and narrower margins undermine the company's ability to absorb fixed R&D/OpEx and may delay sustainable profitability even as design wins convert to production.

bear.t: Audit adjustments, filing extension and governance friction
bear.b: Audit adjustments and filing delays, coupled with historical internal control notes, create durable governance and reporting risk that can hinder capital raising and lender confidence. Such issues increase compliance costs, may restrict financing options, and can materially delay strategic initiatives over multiple reporting cycles.
